results.note: Cultural Survival, Aug 5, 2026: the 48 Cantones is a Maya K'iche' ancestral authority of community governments whose representatives are 'elected annually in assembly'. The page never says 'open' assembly; removed that qualifier and reworded.
results.text: In Totonicapán, the 48 Cantones is a K'iche' ancestral authority built from community governments, with representatives chosen each year in assembly.
results.evidence: community governments whose representatives are elected annually in assembly

results.note: Cultural Survival, Oct 25, 2012: the 48 Cantones' sustainable forest and water management 'has been an example for communities all over Guatemala'. Statement dates from 2012; as_of null acceptable.

Cultural Survival Quarterly, Mar 2, 2022: Court announced its decision on Dec 17, 2021 in Maya Kaqchikel Peoples of Sumpango vs. Guatemala, finding violations of freedom of expression; reparations cover four affected communities, so 'and other communities' holds.

Cultural Survival 2020 grant list: Naköj 'has been working since 2013'; the grant project's productions are in Kaqchikel and Spanish; it benefits 7,000 Kaqchikel listeners. Page does not say it has broadcast in both languages since 2013; tightened wording.
results.text: Community Radio Naköj in Santo Domingo Xenacoj, working since 2013, produces programs in Kaqchikel and Spanish for about 7,000 Kaqchikel listeners.
results.evidence: The project benefits 7,000 radio listeners of the Mayan Kaqchikel people

results.note: Page (Mar 2022) names José Francisco Calí Tzay (Maya Kaqchikel) as UN Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples. Past tense 'served' is appropriate today.
Cultural Survival 2019 grants page: Radio Chiquixji, Alta Verapaz, serves a bilingual Q'eqchi'/Spanish population and a monolingual Q'eqchi' community.

Cultural Survival, May 8, 2018: CCJ, Belize's highest appellate court, affirmed (April 2015) that the 39 Q'eqchi and Mopan communities have rights to lands they customarily used. Facts correct, but original copied 8 consecutive words ('rights to the lands they have customarily used'); reworded.
results.text: In southern Belize, 39 Q'eqchi' and Mopan Maya communities have rights to their customary lands, as Belize's highest appeals court affirmed in 2015.
results.evidence: 39 Q'eqchi and Mopan Maya Indigenous communities of southern Belize

results.note: Cultural Survival 2019 grants page: B'alam Stereo, Cabricán, serving the Maya Mam since 1976; 'their work has strongly promoted education, health, water and justice'. Original copied 7 consecutive words ('one of the older Indigenous radio stations in') and said 'programs on'; reworded to match.
results.text: B'alam Stereo in Cabricán, among the longer-running Indigenous stations in Guatemala's highlands, has served the Maya Mam since 1976, with work promoting education, health, water and justice.
results.evidence: serving the Maya Mam population since 1976

results.note: Cultural Survival, Feb 2, 2026: in October 2025 Maya Kaqchikel de Sumpango, Maya Achí Chicaj, Mam de Cajolá and Maya Mam de Todos Santos Cuchumatán submitted an alternative report to CERD on community radio rights.
Cultural Survival, Mar 21, 2013: Radio Sembrador in San Pedro La Laguna on Lake Atitlán airs programs in Spanish and Tz'utujil, including a Tz'utujil news program on political and cultural issues.

Cultural Survival, Dec 10, 2013: youth from Guatemala, Belize and El Salvador (conference Nov 26-28, 2013) visited Santiago and the home of the local traditional authority, who described the role of ancestral authorities, speaking in Tz'utujil.

Cultural Survival, Aug 26, 2020, by an Ixil author: the Q'imb'al Ixil weavers women's initiative, with the youth group Q'asab Yol and community ancestral authorities, built and inaugurated Radio Tiichajil Tenam (Dec 29, 2019) in Nebaj to inform communities about cultural values.

Cultural Survival, Aug 28, 2020: Constitutional Court (exp. 3883-2017) granted amparo to the Maya Ixil people of Nebaj over Ak'ul land, recognized their ownership and ordered state titles cancelled; notified July/Aug 2020.

Maya Leaders Alliance statement on Cultural Survival (Apr 2015): CCJ judgment 'requires the government to demarcate and register Maya village lands, and protect them against incursions by outsiders'. Content correct, but original copied 10 consecutive words; reworded.
results.text: A 2015 Caribbean Court of Justice judgment obliges Belize's government to mark out and register Maya village lands in the south and guard them against outsiders.
results.evidence: requires the government to demarcate and register Maya village lands

results.note: CCJ President's closing remarks (Oct 30, 2025): Protocol adopted January 2022 and a 'working draft' on Recognition and Protection of Maya Customary Land Tenure adopted September 2025. Page does not say the Maya adopted it themselves, nor that the draft is a law; corrected.
results.text: In 2022 a Free, Prior and Informed Consultation Protocol for the Maya of southern Belize was adopted, and in 2025 a working draft on protecting Maya customary land tenure followed.
results.evidence: adoption in January 2022 of the Maya of Southern Belize Free Prior

results.note: UNESCO ICH page: 'Today, Garifuna communities mainly live in Honduras, Guatemala, Nicaragua and Belize'; language belongs to the Arawakan group. Content correct, but the first clause was a near-verbatim copy of a 10-word sentence; reworded.
results.text: Most Garifuna communities today are in Honduras, Guatemala, Nicaragua and Belize, and the Garifuna language is part of the Arawakan family.
results.evidence: Garifuna communities mainly live in Honduras, Guatemala, Nicaragua and Belize

results.note: UNESCO ICH page: 'Inscribed in 2008 (3.COM) on the Representative List ... (originally proclaimed in 2001)'.
Government of Belize press release PR#234-23 (Oct 25, 2023): 2024 public and bank holidays include Tuesday 19th November, Garifuna Settlement Day.

CSQ 50-3, Sep 15, 2026, Guna authors: Guna General Congress connects the 49 communities of Gunayala and is 'our highest political and administrative body', addressing territory, natural resources and education.

Same page: territory on Panama's Caribbean coast to the Colombian border; coastline about 315 km with more than 400 small islands and islets. Figures correct; original copied 7 consecutive words ('more than 400 small islands and islets'); lightly reworded.
results.text: Gunayala runs along Panama's Caribbean coast to the Colombian border, with about 315 km of coastline and over 400 small islands and islets.
results.evidence: Its coastline is approximately 315 kilometers long and includes more than 400

results.note: Page: autonomy 'did not originate from a State law' and self-governance 'existed long before its formal legal recognition'; Law 16 of Feb 19, 1953 organized the Comarca of San Blas, now Gunayala. 'Older than any state law' overstated this; corrected.
results.text: Guna authors note that their self-government existed long before any state law recognized it; Panama's Law 16 of 1953 legally organized the comarca now called Gunayala.
results.evidence: Law 16, enacted on February 19, 1953, legally organized

results.note: FAOLEX copy of Ley 22 (Oct 20, 1983): creates the Comarca Emberá in Darién; Art. 10 makes the comarca General Congress the 'máximo organismo tradicional de decisión y expresión del pueblo Emberá'.

UNICEF LAC page: the songs text is listed 'para las escuelas EIB'; the bilingual Emberá/Spanish storybooks are described as a base for the education of Emberá children at the initial (early) level. Corrected to match.
results.text: Bilingual storybooks in Emberá and Spanish are among the learning materials made for the early education of Emberá children in Panama.
results.evidence: Libros de cuentos bilingües en lengua emberá y español

results.note: INEC Panama Censo 2023, Cuadro 20 national totals: Ngäbe 444,878; Kuna (Guna) 112,319; Emberá 51,657; next is Buglé 23,898. Third largest is correct.
La Estrella de Panamá, 03/04/2022: Aulina Ismare Opua elected Cacica Nacional del Pueblo Wounaan at the XIII Congreso Ordinario Nacional del Pueblo Wounaan in Taimatí-Cemaco.

Yale e360, May 5, 2022: technicians used smartphone mapping software and GIS; it was the Wounaan of Majé community that submitted the complaint to the Wounaan National Congress (which filed with MiAmbiente), not the technicians. Corrected attribution.
results.text: Wounaan forest technicians map illegal clearing with smartphone apps and GIS, and communities bring that evidence to the Wounaan National Congress.
results.evidence: Wounaan technicians had used mapping software on their smartphones

results.note: INEC Censo 2023 Cuadro 20: Wounaan 10,634 (5,392 men, 5,242 women).
INEC Censo 2023 Cuadro 20: Ngäbe 444,878 of 698,114 Indigenous people; next largest is Kuna at 112,319.
FAOLEX copy of Ley 10 (Mar 7, 1997): Art. 1 creates the Comarca Ngöbe-Buglé; Art. 9 makes its lands collective property and prohibits private appropriation and alienation.

INEC Censo 2023 Cuadro 20: Buglé 23,898 nationally; within 'Comarca Ngäbé Buglé' the table lists Ngäbe 194,938 and Buglé 12,027. The table says nothing about self-government; replaced that with what the table shows.
results.text: Panama's 2023 census counted 23,898 Buglé people; about 12,000 of them live in the Ngäbe-Buglé comarca, which they share with the Ngäbe.

results.note: Ley 10 (1997) Art. 17 recognizes the comarca General Congress as 'máximo organismo de expresión y decisión étnica y cultural del pueblo ngöbe-buglé'. Original broadened this to all collective decisions; narrowed to the law's wording.
results.text: Under Panama's 1997 comarca law, the comarca's General Congress is the highest body for the ethnic and cultural voice and decisions of the Ngäbe-Buglé people.
results.evidence: máximo organismo de expresión y decisión étnica y cultural del pueblo ngöbe-buglé

results.note: Mongabay, Feb 2021: 1,600 sq km Naso Tjër Di comarca, 'result of a decades-long effort to secure the Naso's land rights'; official on Dec 4, 2020.
Mongabay: President Cortizo went to Sieyik, 'where the Naso's king resides', to sign the legislation (Dec 4, 2020); Reynaldo Santana is named king of the Naso.
INEC Censo 2023 Cuadro 20: Naso 5,568. Note: the census lists 'Teribe' (1,331) as a separate answer category.
DIPALICORI (UCR): Bribri spoken on the Atlantic slope (Talamanca, Limón) and Pacific slope (Buenos Aires, Puntarenas) of the Talamanca range; three varieties named for Amubre, Coroma and Salitre.

DIPALICORI: 1978 editions published by the Universidad de Costa Rica, open access, free to read and download. Supported; only change is the title spelling, which the page gives as BIYÖCHŐKNAME (second o is ő).
results.text: In 1978 the University of Costa Rica published Biyöchőkname, a cultural periodical in the Bribri language; its issues are now free to read online.
results.evidence: ediciones del periódico publicadas en 1978 por la Universidad de Costa Rica

results.note: INEC Censo 2023 Cuadro 20: Bri Bri 766 (372 men, 394 women).

DIPALICORI: 2011 census, 87.6% of the population of the official territories (about 11,133) speak Cabécar. 'A strong living language' is not on the page, which rates it safe in Talamanca and definitely endangered in Buenos Aires; replaced with the page's rating.
results.text: Costa Rica's 2011 census found that 87.6 percent of people in the official Cabécar territories, about 11,133 people, speak Cabécar; it is rated safe in Talamanca.
results.evidence: habla el idioma el 87,6% de la población de los territorios oficiales

results.note: TEC Anexo 6 (2013): Cabécar in 9 territories (Talamanca Cabécar, Alto Chirripó, Bajo Chirripó, Nairí Awari, Ujarrás, China Kichá, Tayni, Telire, Keköldi), more than Bribri (4) or Ngäbe (5).
Cultural Survival (es), Mar 20, 2025, by COPINH staff: community-based organization of the Lenca people, present in 5 departments of Honduras, working 'Por 30 años'.
Same page: COPINH's 4 community radios share bulletins, correspondence, podcasts, interviews, trainings and radio programs with Lenca communities.
Cultural Survival, Jun 29, 2021: correspondent training 'for 24 Lenca women and 17 men' began during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Cultural Survival, Jul 29, 2021: stations reach 17 Indigenous territories, 154 communities, 95 percent Miskitu; YATAMA operates three stations. The page's own related items (2024, Jun 2026) report YATAMA's leader died in state custody, so present tense is unsafe; dated to 2021.
results.text: In 2021 the Yapti Tasba community radio network, linked to Miskitu organization YATAMA, reached 17 Indigenous territories and 154 communities, 95 percent of them Miskitu.
results.evidence: reach 17 Indigenous territories, covering a total of 154 communities

results.note: Same page: Law 28 establishes that Indigenous inhabitants of the Caribbean Coast communities have the right to maintain and develop their languages, religions and cultures, and to bilingual education.

Cultural Survival, Sep 20, 2013: on Sep 12, 2013 Honduras granted more than 1.6 million acres of coastal lands to the Miskito; title to seven land areas comprising 128 communities. Facts correct, but original copied about 8 consecutive words; reworded.
results.text: In 2013 Honduras titled over 1.6 million acres of coastal land in La Moskitia to the Miskitu, in seven land areas that include 128 communities.
results.evidence: 1.6 million acres of coastal lands to the Indigenous Miskito people

results.note: Cultural Survival, Aug 29, 2022: Bosawas, in the Mosquitia, is 'a territory with recognized ancestral rights of the Mayagna and Miskito Peoples'. Content correct, but original copied 8 consecutive words; reworded.
results.text: Nicaragua's Bosawás Biosphere Reserve, in the Mosquitia region, is ancestral territory of the Mayangna and Miskitu peoples, whose rights there are recognized.
results.evidence: a territory with recognized ancestral rights of the Mayagna and Miskito Peoples

results.note: Same page: after hurricanes Iota and Eta (late 2020), communities in Bonanza repaired the roofs of 15 homes collectively in early 2021 and planted 50 plots of basic grains along with beans, corn, cassava and more.

Cultural Survival, Nov 25, 2020: Nahuatl cribs 'created by Nahuat-speaking teachers' where children learn; Santo Domingo operates Radio Sensunat promoting Nahuat Pipil culture and language. 'Language nests' is the researcher's gloss, not on the page; removed.
results.text: In Santo Domingo de Guzmán, Nahuat-speaking teachers created Nahuatl cribs where children learn the language, and Radio Sensunat promotes Nahuat Pipil culture.
results.evidence: Nahuatl cribs are places that have been created by Nahuat-speaking teachers

results.note: Same page: Izalco's Indigenous governing body is made up of mayordomos and mayordomas, and Izalco is 'the only one in the country that has an ancestral Indigenous government' (as of 2020).
Cultural Survival, May 8, 2020: 2014 reform of article 63 of the constitution recognized Indigenous Peoples and committed to policies maintaining their ethnic and cultural identity.
Dominica Division of Culture: represented in parliament by a representative and in the Territory by a Chief and six councilors elected every five years.
Dominica Electoral Office: Anette Thomas-Sanford of Sineku elected Kalinago Chief on July 22, 2024 with 697 votes, 58.28% of votes counted.

Division of Culture: Kalinago Barana Aute promotes traditional Kalinago ways of life; visitors see traditional structures, craft making and cultural performances. Page spells 'Aute' without the circumflex.
UNESCO ICH: system based on reparation and compensation, applied by the Pütchipü'üi (palabreros), experts in resolving disputes between matrilineal clans; inscribed 2010.
UNESCO ICH: 'The Wayuu community inhabits the Guajira Peninsula straddling Colombia and Venezuela.' The page does not call it 'a single territory'; removed that framing.
results.text: The Wayuu live on the Guajira Peninsula, which spans the border between Colombia and Venezuela.
results.evidence: The Wayuu community inhabits the Guajira Peninsula straddling Colombia and Venezuela

results.note: DANE CNPV 2018 La Guajira presentation: 380,460 self-identified Wayúu (270,413 in 2005), up 40.7%; 'El pueblo Wayuu, el más numeroso del país'.
VIDS villages page: four large Indigenous peoples, Kari'na, Lokono, Trio and Wayana; Washabo, Apoera and Alfonsdorp are listed as Lokono villages.

LD&C vol. 9 (2015): participants at a workshop on the common Lokono orthography (representatives of Surinamese and French Guianese villages and VIDS) set up Wadian Bokotothi 'Language Keepers'; it then presented the spelling to Guyanese Lokono (2012). The page does not say founders were 'Lokono speakers'; corrected.
results.text: Lokono village representatives founded Wadian Bokotothi, meaning 'Language Keepers', and helped share one common Lokono spelling across Suriname, French Guiana and Guyana.
results.evidence: to preserve their linguistic and cultural heritage, called Wadian Bokotothi

results.note: VIDS, Sep 4, 2026: on Aug 31, 2026 VIDS presented a resolution calling on the government to fully implement the Kaliña and Lokono judgment and enact legislation protecting ancestral living areas.
VIDS villages page: District Marowijne, 24. Christiaankondre (Galibi) and 25. Langamankondre (Galibi), both Kari'na, each with a named village head.

VIDS, Sep 4, 2026: legal recognition of collective rights is 'geen beleidskeuze maar een noodzakelijke verplichting'; calls for full implementation of the Kaliña and Lokono judgment. Note: overlaps heavily with lokono-guianas fact 2 (same source and event).
